name: Verelyn
tagline: Journalist agents that write your morning briefing
description: The newsletters you pay for are good, and they were written for thousands of people at once, which is why most of them sit unopened. Verelyn is a newsroom built around one reader. Its journalist agents read your sources every morning, fold four reports of the same thing into a single event with its sources attached, weigh each one against what you actually have riding on this week, and send one briefing at 07:00. Every item is signed by the agent who wrote it and carries its sources, including where they disagree. Most events get dropped and the reason is recorded, so a miss can be answered for. Hayes covers the first beat, startups and AI. Live since August 2026, and the first reader paid twelve days after the first commit.

name: Flare
description: An agent that keeps you close to your friends. It tells you what they're up to in near-real-time, and telling it about your life is the same act that feeds theirs. The whole product is one conversation: you open it and the Orb is already talking, your answer is your check-in, and it closes by pointing you at a real human. No likes, no comments, no feed of strangers. Live on iOS. I designed and built the system: 29 database tables with row-level security, 23 Edge Functions, three AI agents on a two-layer pipeline.

name: Privé
description: Creators sell digital content, video calls and VIP group access without leaving Telegram. They get paid through Mercado Pago, crypto or bank transfer, and the money lands in their account, never mine. Privé charges 0% on every plan and every method, and makes its money on the Premium subscription instead of a cut of each sale. Bot, mini app, payment rails and the fee engine are all mine.

name: Inception
tagline: Bitcoin mining farm with over 500k in ASICs
description: Started this at 21. We host and operate our own mining rigs, built the infrastructure, automated the operations, and scaled it into a real business. Still running today, still generating revenue, and it funds everything else I build.

name: Stevay
description: A construction company's data is scattered across ERPs, spreadsheets and WhatsApp, and none of it lines up until the year closes. Stevay sat on top and read it as it arrived, then structured the administrative work and ran it: 75+ agents across finances, documentation, purchasing, progress, certification, management and communication. Nothing new to adopt, and a human signed off on anything that touched money. I co-founded it with Franco Quattroqui and owned tech and product. We shipped it, then stopped taking it forward.

name: DL3ARN
description: We built a SaaS to make academic credentials verifiable on-chain. Great team, real leads from universities, a product that worked. Then the crypto bear market hit and made fundraising impossible. I learned more from this one than from anything that succeeded.

name: Clikan
description: A mobile app where you collect and share real-world spots. Taught me everything about social mechanics, location APIs, and thinking mobile-first. The product didn't survive, but the lessons did.

name: Aequsy
description: A platform where you could win prizes while supporting real causes. I got deep into payments, conversion funnels, and building for a mission bigger than the product itself.

name: Bloorfy
description: My first real coding project. I built it to learn web development and ended up learning what it actually takes to ship something. Messy code, zero users, but it changed my trajectory.
